title: Loop Invariant for Summing a Prefix

guide.problem: Find an answer without inventing an input value.
guide.design: A scan keeps a small fact about the visited prefix. A library algorithm is shorter when its contract already matches.
guide.invariant: The stored answer describes only the items already visited.
guide.failure: An initial maximum of zero gives the wrong answer for all-negative input. Replacing < with <= changes first-maximum tie behavior.
guide.trace: For [3,9,9,2], the first maximum index moves from 0 to 1, then stays 1.
guide.maintenance: Keep empty-input and tie rules explicit so a caller can rely on them.
guide.scope: This panel connects this listing to its chapter’s problem. Short demonstrations illustrate one part; the chapter’s complete implementation and invariant labs test the broader contract.

experiment: Predict one boundary or tie case, then change this listing and trace the affected state. For [3,9,9,2], the first maximum index moves from 0 to 1, then stays 1.
